entities.summary: Reginald of Orleans, OP was an Italian Dominican friar and Catholic priest who played a pivotal role in the early years of the Dominican Order. Born in a region of Italy that would later become a central hub for the Catholic Church, Reginald was one of the first members and a close collaborator of Saint Dominic. In 1216, Reginald co-founded the Dominican priory in Bologna, Italy, which would serve as a model for the Order's future growth. Through his tireless work in spreading the teachings of Saint Dominic, Reginald helped establish the Dominican Order as a major force in European society during the 13th century. His legacy as a key figure in the development of the Order continues to influence Catholic theology and practice to this day. Reginald's commitment to the Dominican charism, which emphasizes preaching, teaching, and preaching, left a lasting impact on the intellectual and spiritual landscape of Western Europe.
